label: late-original-phase input q (positions 5-8), gated by sequence-initial token
explanation: Fires only at the end of the original phase (orig_idx 5-8, ~96% of mass) or on the <DEL> step (~4%); it never fires in the copy phase or at t<4. Input q is the dominant trigger (62% of mass, 15x lift) and gives the strongest activations: every top example is a q at position 6-7, often right after j (prev_tok j has 8x lift). Activation is more likely in longer sequences (L=8-9) and depends on the first original token: l, 3, 2, z have the highest lift and c/d/u/k/b/p rarely fire. Even so, most q inputs at late positions do not fire (q & orig_idx>=5 has precision 0.14), and about 40% of the mass sits on other late-position inputs (a, w, u, h, <DEL> ...). Adding the first-token condition only brings dev F1 to about 0.36 (mass recall 0.51). This looks like a distributed hidden-state code (late position x q x sequence context) that a simple token predicate cannot capture.
